title: Set up Release Please and package publishing workflow
description: This repo has no release workflow. Every package.json has private: true, there are no GitHub Actions workflows, no GitHub releases, and no npm/bun packages published. Set up automated release and publishing using Release Please. Scope: (1) Add Release Please GitHub Action workflow (.github/workflows/release-please.yml) configured for Bun monorepo with conventional commits; (2) Configure release-please-config.json and .release-please-manifest.json for all 5 workspace packages (cli, shared, mcp, platform-claude-code, platform-opencode); (3) Determine which packages should be public vs private — at minimum @phil-ai/cli and @phil-ai/mcp need publishing for end-user consumption; shared may need publishing if external packages depend on it; platform generators may stay private; (4) Add publish workflow that triggers after Release Please creates a release — runs bun test, bun run build, then npm publish for public packages; (5) Configure package.json files for publishing: remove private: true from publishable packages, add files/exports/publishConfig/repository fields, add prepublishOnly script for build verification; (6) Set up GITHUB_TOKEN and NPM_TOKEN secrets for CI; (7) Add changeset or conventional commit linting to enforce Release Please conventions; (8) Consider whether the MCP server should also be distributed as a standalone binary (bun build --compile). Acceptance criteria: pushing a conventional commit to main triggers Release Please PR, merging that PR creates GitHub release + publishes packages to npm.

title: Add registry.jsonc generation to OpenCode generator
description:
Add OCX registry manifest generation to the existing OpenCode generator pipeline.

## What
Add a generateRegistry() function to platforms/opencode/generator/index.ts that produces a registry.jsonc at the repo root. This manifest lists all 5 skills as OCX components, each pointing to their generated output files in platforms/opencode/output/.

## OCX Registry Format
```jsonc
{
  "\$schema": "https://ocx.kdco.dev/schemas/v2/registry.json",
  "name": "phil-ai",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "author": "pjbeyer",
  "components": [
    {
      "name": "learning",
      "type": "skill",
      "description": "Capture and implement learnings with hierarchical storage",
      "files": [
        "platforms/opencode/output/skills/learning/SKILL.md",
        "platforms/opencode/output/skills/learning/mcp.json"
      ]
    }
    // ... repeat for docs, context, workflow, guide
  ]
}
```

## Implementation
1. Read core skill definitions from core/skills/*/skill.json (already done by generator)
2. Map each skill to an OCX component entry with type=skill
3. Set files[] to the relative paths of generated SKILL.md and mcp.json
4. Write registry.jsonc to repo root
5. Call generateRegistry() from the existing generateAll() pipeline

## Reference
- OCX schema: https://ocx.kdco.dev/schemas/v2/registry.json
- Example: ~/Projects/pjbeyer/ocx/examples/registry-starter/registry.jsonc
- Existing generator: platforms/opencode/generator/index.ts

## Acceptance
- registry.jsonc validates against OCX schema
- All 5 skills listed with correct relative file paths
- Generated as part of 'phil-ai generate' command
- Existing marketplace.json generation unchanged
close_reason: Implemented: platforms/opencode/generator/registry.ts created, generateAll() updated, registry.jsonc generated at repo root with 5 OCX components. Tests pass.

title: Epic: Unified distribution hub — marketplace + OCX registry
description:
Make phil-ai serve as both a Claude Code marketplace AND an OpenCode OCX registry for all phil-ai skills/plugins.

## Goal
Users can install phil-ai plugins via EITHER:
- Claude Code: claude plugin marketplace add pjbeyer/phil-ai  
- OpenCode: ocx registry add pjbeyer/phil-ai, then ocx add phil-ai/<skill>

## Current State
- Claude Code marketplace: DONE (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json exists, lists 4 plugins)
- OpenCode OCX registry: NOT DONE (no registry.jsonc, no generated registry artifacts)
- CLI has 2 stub commands (update, sync) and 2 registration stubs that are obsolete

## Architecture
Phil-ai already has generators for both platforms:
- platforms/claude-code/generator/ → produces marketplace.json + individual plugin manifests
- platforms/opencode/generator/ → produces unified plugin with all skills (prod + dev)

The main gap: OpenCode generator doesn't produce a registry.jsonc manifest. Adding this is straightforward — it's a JSON file listing components with relative file paths.

## OCX Registry Format
registry.jsonc: { name, version, author, components: [{ name, type, description, files: [relative paths] }] }
Schema: https://ocx.kdco.dev/schemas/v2/registry.json

## Success Criteria
- registry.jsonc exists at repo root, generated by phil-ai generate
- All 5 skills listed as OCX components pointing to generated output files  
- marketplace.json continues to work for Claude Code
- Obsolete CLI code removed
- Documentation updated with both installation methods
close_reason: Epic complete: All 4 sub-issues closed. registry.jsonc generated, CLI cleaned, validate extended, docs updated. bun test: 69 pass, 0 fail.

title: Extend config inventory and drift detection for AI tool configs
description:
Phil-ai's drift detection (shared/src/drift/) and planned snapshot (pai-a1i) currently cover phil-ai's own data dirs and plugin state. They need to extend to cover the full AI tool config landscape for integration with chezmoi dotfiles management.

New inventory targets:
- ~/.config/opencode/ — profiles, plugins, model assignments, oh-my-opencode.json, ocx.jsonc
- ~/.config/opencode/profiles/*/ — per-profile overrides (8 profiles: bedrock, contributor, copilot, default, demo, ollama, vanilla, vertex)
- ~/.claude/ — Claude Code skills, rules, settings
- ~/.config/phil-ai/ — systems.yaml, config.yaml
- Per-repo .opencode/ directories — project-level skills, commands, plugins (cross-ref with scaffold output)
- Per-repo .claude-plugin/ directories — project-level Claude Code plugins

New drift detectors to add to shared/src/drift/detectors/:
- config-inventory: census all AI tool config files, report what exists where
- profile-consistency: detect when OpenCode profiles have conflicting or stale model assignments
- skill-duplication: detect same skill installed globally AND per-project (shadowing)
- absolute-path-drift: detect MCP configs with hardcoded paths that don't resolve on current machine
- secret-exposure: detect unencrypted secrets in config files that should be age-encrypted via chezmoi

Output format: structured JSON that can be consumed by chezmoi templates (.chezmoidata.yaml) or the Phil AI Notion hub. This is the bridge between phil-ai (knows what configs should look like) and chezmoi (ensures they're in place).

Depends on: pai-a1i (/phil-ai-snapshot) for the inventory infrastructure. Related: workspace issue for chezmoi integration design.

title: Documentation review: CLI help, README clarity, and local dev walkthrough
description:
Current docs have several gaps that make it hard for someone (including the maintainer) to understand and use phil-ai effectively. Seven areas to address:

(1) CLI help text needs purpose and output info — each command (install, status, generate, validate, scaffold, guide) should explain WHY you'd run it and WHAT it produces, not just parameter descriptions. Help text should orient the user: 'am I setting up, maintaining, monitoring, or building?'

(2) README should link to docs/ for deeper info — the README currently tries to cover too much inline. Add a docs/ section index and link to it. README should be a quick orientation, not a reference manual.

(3) README over-describes phil-ai-* plugins — each plugin repo (phil-ai-workflow, phil-ai-learning, etc.) has its own description and README. The phil-ai README should reference them briefly with links, not repeat their contents.

(4) CLI usage scenarios need framing — unclear when to reach for which command. Needs a usage matrix or decision tree: setup (install, scaffold), maintenance (validate, guide), monitoring (status + MCP verification tools), new development (generate, scaffold). Make it obvious which commands are for first-time setup vs ongoing use.

(5) 'generate' command purpose is unclear — what does it generate, why, when do you run it, and what do you do with the output? Currently described as 'Generate platform plugins to .claude-plugin/' which raises more questions than it answers.

(6) Scaffold vs Generate relationship needs explicit documentation — these serve fundamentally different purposes but their names suggest overlap. scaffold takes an EXISTING Claude Code plugin and adds OpenCode compatibility files. generate runs INSIDE this repo to build phil-ai's own distribution artifacts. The generated scaffold code contains a dual-path loader pattern (isLocalPlugin check in templates.ts) that auto-detects whether it's running from .opencode/plugin/ (local dev) or dist/ (published npm). This pattern is the backbone of the local dev experience and is completely undocumented outside of specs/002-scaffold-command/.

(7) Add docs/local-dev-walkthrough.md — step-by-step guide for locally testing this plugin alongside other phil-ai-* plugins in both Claude Code and OpenCode. Should cover: the dual-path loader pattern and why it exists, how .opencode/plugin/ auto-discovery works, linking/installing the MCP server locally, configuring OpenCode skills to point at local builds, testing CLI commands against real plugin repos, verifying MCP tools work end-to-end, and debugging common issues (wrong paths, stale builds, missing data dirs).

title: Git State Adapter (read-only)
description: Create shared/src/adapters/git.ts — a READ-ONLY adapter that queries git state for verification purposes. Does NOT create branches, commits, or PRs (that's phil-ai-workflow's job). Functions: getActiveBranches(profileDirs) → finds feature branches across profiles (mirrors phil-ai-workflow's /work-status logic), getBranchAge(branch) → days since last commit, isMerged(branch, target) → checks merge status, getRecentCommits(branch, count) → commit history. Used by drift detection (stale branches), pattern detection (velocity from commits), and dashboard (active work summary). Respects phil-ai-workflow's profile model: work, pjbeyer, play, home.
close_reason: Read-only git adapter: getActiveBranches, getBranchAge, isMerged, getRecentCommits in shared/src/adapters/git.ts

title: Implement Metrics Collection
description: Create shared/src/metrics/ module for tracking and aggregating workflow metrics. Duration tracking: calculate actualDuration from startedAt/completedAt. Velocity: items completed per week over configurable rolling window (default 4 weeks). Scorecard aggregation: compute each of the 10+1 dimensions from raw data — e.g., waste_level from stale items count, improvement_rate from closed gate failures → fixes, lead_time from avg duration. MetricsStore: persist snapshots to dataDir/workflow/metrics/{period}.json. queryMetrics(dateRange) for trend analysis.
close_reason: Metrics collection: duration pairing, velocity (0 for empty), scorecard aggregation, MetricsStore with file locking

title: Add registry.jsonc validation to validate command
description:
Extend the existing CLI validate command to also validate the generated registry.jsonc against the OCX schema.

## What
The validate command (cli/src/commands/validate/index.ts) currently validates marketplace.json and plugin.json structures using Zod schemas. Add OCX registry validation:

1. Load registry.jsonc from repo root
2. Validate against OCX schema (https://ocx.kdco.dev/schemas/v2/registry.json)
3. Verify all referenced files[] actually exist at the specified paths
4. Report validation results alongside existing marketplace/plugin validation

## Also
- Add registry validation to tests/validate-plugin.sh (the comprehensive validation script)
- Ensure 'phil-ai validate' covers both marketplace.json AND registry.jsonc in one pass

## Acceptance
- validate command checks registry.jsonc when present
- File existence checks for all component files[]
- Schema validation against OCX spec
- Clear error messages for validation failures
- validate-plugin.sh includes registry checks
close_reason: Implemented: RegistryComponentSchema and RegistrySchema added to validate/index.ts. validateRegistry() function added. detectValidationType() updated for .jsonc. bunx phil-ai validate registry.jsonc exits 0.

title: Update README with dual-distribution installation docs
description:
Update the phil-ai README to document both installation methods: Claude Code marketplace and OpenCode OCX registry.

## What
Add clear installation instructions for both platforms:

### Claude Code Users
```
claude plugin marketplace add pjbeyer/phil-ai
claude plugin install learning@phil-ai
claude plugin install docs@phil-ai
# etc.
```

### OpenCode Users
```
ocx registry add pjbeyer/phil-ai
ocx add phil-ai/learning
ocx add phil-ai/docs
# etc.
```

## Also Update
- List all 5 available skills with descriptions
- Remove any outdated 'bunx phil-ai install' instructions (if CLI install becomes simplified)
- Mention that both methods install from the same source of truth

## Acceptance
- README has clear dual-platform installation instructions
- Skill catalog with descriptions
- No references to obsolete installation methods
close_reason: Implemented: README.md updated with dual-distribution (Claude Code + OCX) installation instructions, guide plugin added, registry.jsonc in architecture tree, update/sync removed from CLI commands. AGENTS.md updated.

title: Remove obsolete CLI distribution commands
description:
Remove CLI commands and code that are obsolete now that marketplace/registry handles distribution.

## What to Remove

### CLI Commands (full removal)
- cli/src/commands/update/index.ts — v0.2.0 stub, never implemented. Only has backup logic, no actual update functionality. Marketplace/registry handles updates natively.
- cli/src/commands/sync/index.ts — v0.2.0 stub, never implemented. No state sync needed with marketplace/registry.

### Registration Stubs (remove from install command)
- cli/src/commands/install/platforms/claude-code.ts — Phase 5 stub (registerClaudeCode). Claude Code marketplace handles discovery.
- cli/src/commands/install/platforms/opencode.ts — Phase 6 stub (registerOpenCode). OCX registry handles discovery.

### CLI Entry Point
- Remove 'update' and 'sync' command registrations from cli/src/index.ts
- Simplify install command to remove platform registration steps

## What to Keep
- install command (directory creation, config init still useful)
- generate command (essential — produces both platform artifacts)
- validate command (essential — validates plugin structures)
- scaffold command (useful — adds OC support to CC plugins)
- status command (useful — health checks)
- guide command (useful — guide management)

## Acceptance
- update and sync commands removed from CLI
- install command no longer calls registerClaudeCode/registerOpenCode
- CLI builds and runs without errors
- Existing tests still pass
close_reason: Implemented: cli/src/commands/update/, cli/src/commands/sync/, and platform stubs deleted. Imports and switch cases removed from cli/src/index.ts and install/index.ts. docs/cli.md and cli/AGENTS.md updated.

title: Integration Tests — Workflow E2E
description: Create tests/integration/workflow/ directory with end-to-end tests. Test full cycles: (1) Start→Status→Finish via MCP tools, verify gate log entries created; (2) Start→Block→Resume→Finish with state transition validation; (3) Multiple items → velocity calculation → scorecard generation; (4) Pattern detection with seeded anomaly data; (5) Drift sweep with intentionally stale/orphaned data; (6) PDCA review generation from real workflow data; (7) Notion sync round-trip (if Notion credentials available, skip otherwise). Follow conditional execution pattern from tests/integration/opencode/ (ENABLED flag gating). Use headless runner pattern for MCP tool invocation.
